obligations.text: The remote pilot in command holds a remote pilot certificate with a small UAS rating. Anyone else at the flight controls is under the direct supervision of that pilot, who can take direct control immediately.
obligations.title: A remote pilot certificate with a small UAS rating

obligations.text: The remote pilot in command, the person at the controls and any visual observer are able to see the aircraft throughout the flight with vision unaided by any device other than corrective lenses, and either the two pilots or a visual observer keep watching it.
obligations.title: Visual line of sight for the whole flight

obligations.text: At night, the remote pilot in command has completed an initial knowledge test or training under 107.65 after April 6, 2021, and the aircraft shows lighted anti-collision lighting visible for at least 3 statute miles. The same lighting is required during civil twilight.
obligations.title: Anti-collision lighting at night and in civil twilight

obligations.text: Operations in Class B, Class C or Class D airspace, or within the lateral boundaries of the surface area of Class E airspace designated for an airport, have prior authorization from Air Traffic Control.
obligations.title: ATC authorization in controlled airspace

obligations.text: The minimum flight visibility, observed from the control station, is at least 3 statute miles.
obligations.title: Flight visibility of at least 3 statute miles

obligations.text: The aircraft stays at least 500 feet below clouds and at least 2,000 feet horizontally from them.
obligations.title: At least 500 feet below and 2,000 feet horizontally from clouds

obligations.text: URML checks flight targets against the people-occupancy zones the deployment declares. People outside those zones, and the path the aircraft flies between targets, are for the remote pilot in command to watch.
obligations.title: People and flight paths the validator cannot see

program.description: Take off to 150 m: above the manifest's 120 m service ceiling and the FAA Part 107 limit of 400 ft (121.92 m).

errors.message: take_off.altitude (150.0 m) exceeds the strictest declared altitude cap (120.0 m).
errors.suggestion: Reduce altitude to at most 120.0 m, or relax the cap if the deployment allows.

errors.message: 14 CFR 107.51(b): maximum altitude 400 feet (121.92 m) above ground level. take_off.altitude is 150 m; the limit is 121.92 m.
errors.suggestion: Use a value at or below 121.92 m.
